Why start writing in the age of ai

writing 17 Aug 2026

Sentence8 words · 0.0 min

practice helps me to write better and faster

why start a personal blog in the age of ai? short version: i’ve lost the skill. i can’t write any more. it’s been few years since i’ve had to do any serious writing and then ai came along and i don’t have to write anymore. i spit out a couple half formed thoughts and a few seconds later i have a coherant email, complete with emdashes.

it’s a skill i enjoy: the ability to express myself and organize my thoughts. it’s one of the things i love about programming. but i’ve lost it.

i was never a great writer, but now i can barely write. if i don’t use ai, it takes me minutes to write a simple two sentance email response. my typing speed should be the determining factor to how long it takes me to fire off a quick confirmation email. but it’s not. i have to think and struggle to orangize the thoughts in the correct way and then i have launch claude and type “make this make sense: < paste >”. and even that prompt is a half-hearted attempt at organizing my thoughts.

a major part of coding has always been communicatoin. but now i have to communicate with my editor. i find my prompts getting lazier and lazier because it can. i can type nonsenicle things like “alias bad fix” and it will to do it. i’m getting dumber and deminishing in skill while it grows. the ability to organize what i want is slipping further and further from my graps

so i have to write. i have to write code by hand but i also have to write for people; even if it’s just my self. the beauty of writing is have to organize your thoughts. you can hold a thought or concept in your mind but writting forces you to solidify that thought and organize it so you can better recall it. writing exposes the gaps where you glosed over the connections and forces you to fill them to make a thought. sometimes just typing out a problem to a coworker is all you need to form the answer. sometimes when writing and answer to a question is all you need to realize you didn’t have the grasp on the issue you thought you had.

of course i’ll write by hand too. but for some reason writing in f ront of the screen feels like a different skill closely related but also much closer to the distractions that can pull you away.

my inability to write is showing itself. i’m not really sure how to end this so think i’m just going to stop… for now.
